description: The Bihar Education Department has partnered with 11 information technology (IT) companies, including Google Education, to train government schoolteachers in information technology and artificial intelligence (AI), as the state moves to strengthen digital learning and technology-enabled classroom teaching.The training programme will be conducted in batches at the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) campus. School principals will nominate teachers for the sessions, which will focus on practical IT skills and AI applications. The Union government’s skill development department will also support the initiative.Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari said the programme would give particular attention to AI, with the objective of improving teaching quality. The department is targeting January to put the training arrangements in place.The teacher training initiative is part of Bihar’s wider plan to expand technology integration across government schools. The state is preparing to make computer education compulsory from Class 6 from the next academic session. It also plans to introduce smart classrooms in 700 model schools before extending the facility to other government schools in phases.Google To Support AI Training For TeachersSeparately, Bihar’s Department of Science, Technology and Technical Education signed a Statement of Intent with Google on September 29 to strengthen AI-enabled teaching and digital infrastructure.Under the proposed collaboration, Google will provide teacher training in Hindi and English through its Google AI Educator Series. The programme will familiarise teachers with tools such as Gemini and NotebookLM and their applications in lesson planning, classroom instruction and administrative tasks.The partnership also envisages support for digital identities for teachers and technical guidance on developing information and communication technology (ICT) laboratories, connected classrooms, digital libraries and language laboratories.Bihar Plans AI Training For University FacultyBeyond school education, Bihar is also preparing to train faculty members at state universities and constituent colleges in the use of AI for academic and administrative work.The proposed training will cover applications such as lecture planning, question-paper preparation and evaluation of answer scripts. The initiative is linked to the University Grants Commission’s (UGC) Guru Dakshata faculty development programme.Through these parallel initiatives, Bihar is seeking to expand AI adoption across school and higher education, with a focus on equipping teachers and faculty members to use digital tools in teaching, assessment and academic administration.
